items.title: 68003_Eddie Sauter oral history interview
items.q: get Eddie Bert to tell you.

ctx.x: He was the original good soldier schweik (phonetic spelling). Ask Eddie Bert the story, because Eddie was with him through this whole thing. It's very funny; I'm not familiar enough to give the story, but if you ever come out to Bill, get Eddie Bert to tell you.
One story is the lieutenant used to come down and plead, please, come on, show up, so that you can get paid. They were supposed to court martial him or something.

items.title: Eddie Bert interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001
items.q: But Red had a good band in those days. Eddie Sauter wrote for him and a guy by the name of Johnny Thompson, who was studying with Eddie Sauter.

ctx.x: That’s funny, we can’t fit it on the thing so speed it up.

But Red had a good band in those days. Eddie Sauter wrote for him and a guy by the name of Johnny Thompson, who was studying with Eddie Sauter. So we had all good arrangements. And he had double reeds, like oboes, bassoons —
